samples.summary: Server-side per-document authorization still fails open by default (shadow mode), so a viewer-role share link remains write-capable; the new client-side read-only gates bound only this app
samples.evidence: `handleAuth` discards every deny when `this.enforce` is false (line 149-164), and `enforce` is only true when `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true'` (line 115-116) — i.e. off in the default configuration. Attack: hold a viewer-role share link, call `GET /auth/yorkie-token` with the share token to mint a Yorkie token (the payload keeps `typ: 'yorkie-share'`, see `hasAccess`, line 254-265), take the project public key that ships in every visitor's bundle (`VITE_YORKIE_PUBLIC_KEY`, packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:957), attach with a bare Yorkie SDK client and `doc.update(...)` the note. The only refusal (`link.role === 'editor'`, line 262) is computed and then thrown away. Everything this change adds on the client — `readOnlyNoteStore` (packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:93), `EditorState.changeFilter` (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:464) — runs in the attacker's own browser and bounds nothing for a non-cooperating client. The change documents this honestly (README, design docs, the boot warning in `logPosture`) rather than fixing it, so I am reporting the posture, not the documentation: as shipped, an unenforced deployment gives read-only link holders write access. Marked major rather than critical only because it is a pre-existing, deliberately staged rollout default, not something this diff introduced.

samples.summary: Client-influenced Yorkie document key is interpolated unsanitized into the shadow-mode warning, allowing log forging in the very log the mitigation tells operators to read
samples.evidence: `const target = (body?.attributes ?? []).map((attr) => `${attr?.key ?? '?'}:${attr?.verb ?? '?'}`).join(',')` (line 156-158) is spliced into `this.logger.warn(...)` at line 159-161 with no length cap, character allowlist, or newline/CR stripping. `attr.key` originates from the document key the *client* chose at attach time and is logged before `parseYorkieDocKey` has vetted it (parsing happens later, in `checkAttribute`, line 220). If the Yorkie server relays a key containing CR/LF (or simply a very long key), an attacker with any valid token can inject synthetic lines such as `yorkie auth webhook: enforcing per-document access` into the log stream — defeating the boot-posture signal this change adds as the mitigation for shadow mode — or flood the log. I could not confirm from this repo whether the Yorkie server rejects control characters in document keys, hence medium confidence; the fix (JSON-stringify or strip `[\r\n]` and truncate) is cheap either way.

samples.summary: Read-only decision is fail-open on an unexpected share-link role (`role === "viewer"`), unlike the server's fail-closed `role === 'editor'` check
samples.evidence: `const readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer";` (line 44) drives every client-side write gate on this surface — `NotesView`'s `readOnly` (line 118), the `readOnlyNoteStore` wrap (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:152), the engine's `changeFilter`, and the share-token uploader `token && !readOnly` (line 74). `ResolvedShareLink.role` is typed `string` (packages/frontend/src/api/share-links.ts:17) and comes straight from the unauthenticated `/share-links/:token/resolve` response, so any role that is not the literal `"viewer"` (a future `commenter`, a casing difference, a backend that ever returns `null`/`undefined`) yields a fully writable mount and hands an anonymous visitor the upload path. The server-side counterparts are written the safe way round (`link.role === 'editor'` in yorkie-auth.controller.ts:262 and image-share-upload.controller.ts:135), so the two would disagree in favour of the client. Not exploitable today because `share-link.service.ts:77` restricts roles to viewer/editor; the inversion (`readOnly = role !== "editor"`) costs nothing. The line is relocated from the deleted `SharedNotesLayout` in shared-document.tsx, so this is pre-existing shape, newly load-bearing now that this route also gates an uploader on it.

samples.summary: Anonymous viewer-role share-link visitors now get a UI control to turn on the blame gutter, surfacing every past editor's display name and edit timestamps
samples.evidence: The toolbar is mounted for viewers too (line 104-115) and `onShowAuthorsChange={setShowAuthors}` (line 111) is not gated on `readOnly`, so a read-only anonymous visitor can enable the authorship gutter; previously the share route passed no `showAuthors` and relied on a per-browser preference an anonymous visitor would not have set. The names/timestamps come from `getAuthorSpans()`, which is in the reader allowlist of `readOnlyNoteStore` (packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:21) and whose data the CRDT already ships to any attached client, so this is a discoverability change rather than a new protocol-level exposure — but it does hand a share-link recipient the internal edit history of who wrote which line, which a document owner sharing a viewer link may not expect.

verdict.reason: Code is present as described and the exploit chain is reachable. yorkie-auth.controller.ts:115-116 sets enforce=false unless YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE==='true' (documented default false: self-hosting.md:185, backend/README.md:101), and lines 149-164 discard every deny in that mode, returning {allowed:true, reason:'shadow'}. The sole viewer-write refusal (line 262, needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true) is therefore computed and thrown away. Both halves an attacker needs are public: auth.controller.ts:82-90 exposes POST /auth/yorkie-token/share with NO guard, minting a typ:'yorkie-share' token (auth.service.ts:77) from a bare share token, and the project key ships in every visitor's bundle (shared-document.tsx:957). No other guard closes it: the other ENFORCE consumers (template/seed/register-templates.ts:154, template-review.ts:80, template.service.ts:470) gate only the public template tier, and YorkieSignatureGuard only proves the caller is Yorkie. The finding's one error is naming GET /auth/yorkie-token instead of POST /auth/yorkie-token/share for the share path (the controller's own comment at line 90 makes the same slip); this misnames the endpoint but not the capability, so it does not refute. In-lane per the rubric (authorization gate whose deny path is not enforced); pre-existence and honest documentation of the fail-open default are not refutation grounds.

finding.summary: The viewer read-only guarantee this change builds on has no server-side enforcement in the default configuration — the Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow (allow-all) mode, so every gate added here is client-side only
finding.evidence: `this.enforce = configService.get('YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE') === 'true'` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:101) defaults to false, and lines 111-119 then return ALLOW for a computed deny. `hasAccess()` would otherwise be the only thing refusing `link.role === 'viewer'` a write (line 217). Attack: a holder of a viewer-role share link calls `fetchYorkieShareToken(token)` (the frontend already does this at shared-document.tsx:959 and hands the result to the SDK), attaches with any Yorkie client outside the browser UI, and pushes arbitrary text ops to the note — no client-side `changeFilter`, `EditorState.readOnly` or `runHistory` guard is in the path. The diff's own comments (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:435-437, docs/design/notes/notes.md) acknowledge this, which makes it a known rollout state rather than a regression — but this change materially widens the surface that depends on it (a viewer is now given a live editor pane and the full `NoteEditorAPI` via the mounted toolbar), so it is worth restating that the boundary is unenforced by default. Mitigation is deployment-level (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`), not code.

verdict.reason: Every element of the claim checks out against the repository. `this.enforce` defaults to false when YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE is unset (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:115-116), and the shadow branch converts any computed deny into HTTP 200 / allowed:true (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:149-164). The viewer write refusal at yorkie-auth.controller.ts:262 (`needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true`) is the only server-side enforcement of the viewer read-only boundary, so in the default configuration it never takes effect. The attack chain is reachable outside the UI: POST /auth/yorkie-token/share is a public, unguarded endpoint that mints a Yorkie token from any valid share token including a viewer link (auth.controller.ts:82-90), and its own comment defers role validation to the webhook. The frontend already performs this exchange for viewers (shared-document.tsx:705,959), so a viewer holds a replayable credential and can attach with an arbitrary Yorkie client and write. No code-level guard elsewhere makes this unreachable — the only mitigation is a deployment env var, which is not the default; in-repo docs (docs/design/sharing.md:208, docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:201-226, packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:64) corroborate that client-side read-only mounts bound only this app. This is a fail-open default on an access-control gate, squarely in the Security lane; pre-existing status is not a refutation ground.
